2. Explore and visualise

Source: vignettes/explore_and_visualise.Rmd
explore_and_visualise.Rmd

Continue in the session from Query the atlas. obs_lung already holds the respiratory cohort: nine Human Cell Atlas studies, with donor age and harmonised cell-type labels.

This article asks whether those cells separate into the immune and epithelial compartments the later models use. You download a SingleCellExperiment, explore it with the tidyomics packages, and integrate the studies with Harmony. Immune cells should sit apart from epithelial cells on the UMAP, and CD45 should mark that split independently of the harmonised label. The same cells are then shown as a Seurat object.

Download counts for the cohort

get_single_cell_experiment() reads the count matrices for the cells in obs_lung and returns one SingleCellExperiment. Cells are subsampled within sample, and the number of samples is capped, so a few large libraries do not dominate the highly variable genes. The download is capped at 12,000 cells, and one sample does not exceed 100 cells.

max_cells_qc <- 12000L
cells_per_sample_qc <- 100L
n_samples_qc <- 120L

set.seed(42)
samples_qc <- dplyr::distinct(obs_lung, sample_id)
samples_qc <- dplyr::slice_sample(samples_qc, n = min(n_samples_qc, nrow(samples_qc)))

sampled_qc <- obs_lung |>
  dplyr::semi_join(samples_qc, by = "sample_id") |>
  dplyr::group_by(sample_id) |>
  dplyr::slice(sample.int(dplyr::n(), min(cells_per_sample_qc, dplyr::n()))) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()

# Compiling the object takes about 8 minutes.
sce_qc <- sampled_qc |>
  get_single_cell_experiment(assays = "counts")
sce_qc

Building sce_qc takes about 10 minutes. The counts are written to inst/extdata/sce_qc.rds before log-normalisation. Load the file if time is short.

sce_qc <- logNormCounts(sce_qc)

With tidySingleCellExperiment loaded, the object prints as a tibble and accepts dplyr verbs and ggplot2. The underlying assay is unchanged.

sce_qc |>
  dplyr::count(cell_type_unified_ensemble, sort = TRUE)
## # A tibble: 29 × 2

Integrate studies and check the split with CD45

This section asks whether immune and epithelial cells occupy different regions once study is removed from the embedding. Highly variable genes are selected per sample (modelGeneVar(block = sample_id)), so genes that vary within a donor rank above genes that merely differ between libraries (Lun, McCarthy, and Marioni 2016). Harmony then removes the study axis from the PCA (Korsunsky et al. 2019). The UMAP is drawn from that embedding.

CD45 (PTPRC, Ensembl ENSG00000081237) marks haematopoietic cells independently of the harmonised label. After Harmony, immune cells should sit in the high-CD45 region and epithelial cells in the low-CD45 region.

hvgs_qc <- sce_qc |>
  modelGeneVar(block = sce_qc$sample_id) |>
  getTopHVGs(n = 2000)

sce_qc <- sce_qc |>
  runPCA(ncomponents = 30, subset_row = hvgs_qc) |>
  RunHarmony(
    group.by.vars = "dataset_id",
    dims.use = 1:30,
    verbose = FALSE,
    reduction.save = "HARMONY"
  ) |>
  runUMAP(dimred = "HARMONY", n_neighbors = 15)

cd45_id <- "ENSG00000081237" # Ensemble ID for PTPRC

sce_cd45 <- sampled_qc |>
  get_single_cell_experiment(assays = "counts", features = cd45_id) 

sce_qc$cd45 <- NA_real_
i <- match(colnames(sce_qc), colnames(sce_cd45))
sce_qc$cd45[!is.na(i)] <- log1p(
  as.numeric(SummarizedExperiment::assay(sce_cd45, "counts")[1, i[!is.na(i)]])
)

#base::saveRDS(sce_qc,"./cellNexusWorkshop/inst/extdata/sce_qc_batch_corrected.rds", compress="xz")
sce_qc |>
  ggplot(aes(UMAP1, UMAP2, colour = cd45)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.3, alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(option = "magma") +
  coord_equal() +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(colour = "CD45 (PTPRC)")

Exercise 4. Colour the same UMAP by dataset_id.

Solution 
sce_qc |>
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(UMAP1, UMAP2, colour = dataset_id)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 0.3, alpha = 0.6) +
  ggplot2::coord_equal() +
  ggplot2::theme_bw()

Exercise 5. Using sce_qc, count cells per cell_type_unified_ensemble. Which of immune_cell_types are missing from this subsample?

Solution 
sce_qc |>
  dplyr::count(cell_type_unified_ensemble, sort = TRUE)

setdiff(immune_cell_types, unique(sce_qc$cell_type_unified_ensemble))

Open the same table as a Seurat object

get_seurat() reads the same metadata table into a Seurat object. tidyseurat gives that object the tibble interface you just used on the SingleCellExperiment. The rest of the workshop stays with SingleCellExperiment. This demo reads 100 cells from one study.

library(tidyseurat)

one_study <- obs_lung |>
  dplyr::filter(dataset_id == dplyr::first(dataset_id)) |>
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 100)

seurat_demo <- one_study |>
  get_seurat(assays = "counts")
